Title: Valid and invalid login responses
Preconditions: Runtime implementation and isolated test database available; one active employee and one inactive account provisioned through an approved fixture/bootstrap.
Test Data: Synthetic active employee credentials; wrong password; inactive-account credentials; unknown email.
Steps: 1) POST valid credentials to /auth/login. 2) Record status and response fields. 3) Repeat with wrong password, inactive account, and unknown email.
Expected Result: Valid login returns 200 with Bearer session, expires_in=3600, and user. Each invalid/unavailable account attempt returns the generic 401 response without disclosing account existence. No passwords appear in responses or logs.

Title: Session lookup, logout, expiry, and revocation
Preconditions: Runtime implementation and controllable clock/session fixture available; valid employee session issued.
Test Data: Synthetic bearer token; valid protected GET /auth/me; revoked token; expired token at time t+3601 seconds.
Steps: 1) Call /auth/me with a valid token. 2) POST /auth/logout with that token. 3) Call /auth/me with the same token. 4) Repeat using an expired session.
Expected Result: Valid session is accepted; logout returns 204; revoked and expired tokens receive 401 on protected calls with no protected response data.

Title: Password change revokes old sessions
Preconditions: Runtime implementation and two active sessions for the same test employee available; password-change endpoint authenticated.
Test Data: Synthetic current password; different new password of 12 characters; same-as-current password; incorrect current password.
Steps: 1) Change password with correct current and valid new password. 2) Call a protected endpoint with both old sessions. 3) Attempt login with old and new passwords. 4) Attempt invalid same-as-current and wrong-current changes.
Expected Result: Successful change returns 204, revokes both prior sessions, rejects old password, accepts new password, and returns no password. Invalid changes persist no password modification.

Title: One-time first-admin bootstrap
Preconditions: Isolated empty test database and approved operator bootstrap command/secret mechanism available; never use production data.
Test Data: Synthetic bootstrap email/password; second bootstrap attempt with a different synthetic account.
Steps: 1) Run the documented bootstrap on the empty database. 2) Inspect stored user and logs. 3) Run bootstrap again after the first admin exists. 4) Confirm account count and roles.
Expected Result: First run creates exactly one admin with a password hash and no plaintext secret in logs/storage. Second run fails safely and creates no additional account. If CLI/operator contract is still absent, report Blocked with the missing prerequisite.

Title: Role-operation-field permission matrix
Preconditions: Runtime API and fixtures for admin, manager, employee available; test every operation and field permission from docs/Backend_Design.md.
Test Data: Three synthetic users; one client; one record of each business type; 27 declared API operations; role/field matrix.
Steps: 1) For each role, invoke each operation directly through HTTP, not through a UI. 2) Submit role/identity claims in request bodies where schemas permit. 3) Record allowed/denied status and side effects.
Expected Result: Only operations and fields allowed by the documented role matrix succeed. Employee cannot administer users or read reports; manager cannot administer accounts/roles. Caller-supplied role data never changes authority. Denials create no business mutation.

Title: Cross-employee record isolation
Preconditions: Runtime API with employees A/B, manager/admin, and deals/tasks/appointments assigned to each employee.
Test Data: Synthetic employee A and B; one record of each type owned by B; unique IDs; page limits 1 and 20.
Steps: 1) As A, list each business collection using default and explicit limits. 2) As A, GET and PATCH each B-owned ID. 3) As A, submit an attempted reassignment. 4) Repeat GET/list as manager.
Expected Result: Employee A’s lists contain no B-owned records; inaccessible individual records return the documented non-disclosing response and no protected fields. Manager can retrieve them. No denied request changes a record.

Title: Forbidden fields and last-active-admin invariant
Preconditions: Runtime API with one active admin, manager, employee, and current resource ETags available.
Test Data: Employee PATCH with archived=false and owner_id equal to self; sole active admin role demotion and deactivation requests.
Steps: 1) As employee, PATCH a client with archived=false. 2) As employee, PATCH own task with owner_id=self. 3) As sole admin, attempt demotion and deactivation. 4) Re-read records and sessions.
Expected Result: Forbidden field submissions return 403 even when value is unchanged and persist no change. Sole active admin cannot be demoted/deactivated; conflict is returned and an active admin remains. Account role/status changes revoke affected sessions.

Title: Protected and nonexistent IDs have equivalent disclosure
Preconditions: Runtime API with employee A and another employee’s private task available.
Test Data: One B-owned task ID and one well-formed nonexistent UUID.
Steps: 1) As employee A, GET the B-owned task. 2) GET the nonexistent task. 3) Compare status and safe problem-response shape/body fields.
Expected Result: Both responses are 404 with equivalent non-disclosing error structure; neither reveals the protected task or whether it exists. Route/field-level forbidden cases remain 403 as specified.

Title: Account administration and minimal assignment directory
Preconditions: Runtime API with all three roles and active/inactive synthetic users available.
Test Data: Synthetic users with distinct display names and emails; duplicate email; unsupported role value.
Steps: 1) As manager and employee, call GET/POST/PATCH /users. 2) As each role, GET /users/directory. 3) As admin, create duplicate-email and unsupported-role accounts. 4) Inspect returned directory properties.
Expected Result: Only admins administer accounts. Each authenticated role sees only active directory IDs/display names; no email, role, or inactive users leak. Duplicate email and unsupported role are rejected without creating an account.

Title: Client create, search, validation, and pagination
Preconditions: Runtime API and authenticated accounts for each role available; empty isolated client fixture.
Test Data: Synthetic display name; nullable email/phone; invalid phone; malformed email; names at 200 and 201 characters; literal % and _; cursor limit 1/100.
Steps: 1) Create a valid client as each role using unique Idempotency-Key values. 2) Search by case-insensitive substring and literal wildcard characters. 3) List with limits 1 and 100 and follow cursors. 4) Submit invalid/overlength fields and unknown JSON property.
Expected Result: Valid clients return 201 with Location and ETag; search is literal and case-insensitive; page limits/cursors behave as specified. Invalid fields, unknown properties, and invalid cursors are rejected without persistence.

Title: Client update, stale ETag, archive, and restore
Preconditions: Runtime API with active client linked to existing historical deal/task/appointment and current ETag available.
Test Data: Synthetic contact update; stale and missing If-Match; admin/manager archive and restore; employee archive PATCH.
Steps: 1) Update contact data with current ETag. 2) Repeat with stale ETag and then missing If-Match. 3) Archive and verify history remains. 4) Attempt a new related record. 5) Restore; try archive as employee.
Expected Result: Current update succeeds and increments version. Stale/missing preconditions return 412/428 without change. Archive preserves existing history and blocks new linked records; permitted restore works; employee archive request returns 403.

Title: Deal creation and decimal/currency boundaries
Preconditions: Runtime API with active client, active owner, configured deployment currency, and role accounts available.
Test Data: Synthetic valid deal; amount 0; 12 integer digits plus 2 decimal digits; negative amount; >12 integer digits; >2 fractional digits; mismatched currency; inactive client/owner.
Steps: 1) Create valid deals with boundary-valid amounts. 2) Attempt each invalid amount/currency/reference and blank or >200-character title. 3) Re-read stored values.
Expected Result: Valid deals return 201 with initial stage new and exact amount representation. Invalid title, precision, negative amount, currency, inactive/missing references, or unauthorized owner is rejected with no row created.

Title: Deal stage timestamps and optimistic update
Preconditions: Runtime API with owned deal and current ETag available.
Test Data: Transitions new->qualified->won->lost->new; current, stale, and missing If-Match; attempts to modify client_id/currency.
Steps: 1) Apply each transition with the latest ETag and read after each. 2) PATCH without stage change. 3) Submit stale and missing ETags. 4) Attempt immutable client/currency changes.
Expected Result: Closed stages set server-generated closed_at; open stages clear it; no stage change preserves it. Immutable fields cannot change. Stale/missing versions return 412/428 and leave resource/version untouched.

Title: Task creation, scope, optional fields, and validation
Preconditions: Runtime API with active client, active/inactive owners, and employee/manager/admin accounts available.
Test Data: Synthetic task title at 1, 200, and 201 characters; owner self/other; optional client/due_at null; inactive or unknown references.
Steps: 1) Create valid task as employee for self and as manager for an active assignee. 2) Read/list tasks. 3) Attempt employee assignment to another user, inactive references, blank/overlength title.
Expected Result: Valid tasks return 201 with todo status and correct optional fields. Invalid or unauthorized creates are rejected without writes. Employee list/query scope is applied before pagination.

Title: Task status timestamps and stale update handling
Preconditions: Runtime API with owned task and current ETag available.
Test Data: todo->in_progress->done->todo->cancelled; stale/missing ETags; nullable due_at.
Steps: 1) Transition through statuses using current ETag and read after each. 2) Clear due_at with null. 3) Repeat a PATCH with stale and missing If-Match.
Expected Result: Entering done sets server completed_at; leaving done clears it; unchanged status preserves it; null due date clears only that field. Invalid preconditions return 412/428 with no update.

Title: Appointment time, timezone, duration, and filter boundaries
Preconditions: Runtime API with active client and employee available; deterministic timezone database.
Test Data: Valid UTC and +05:00 offsets; past appointment; zero/negative interval; exactly 24-hour and >24-hour intervals; missing offset; invalid IANA zone; appointment filter intervals 366 days and 366 days plus one second.
Steps: 1) Create appointments for valid offset, past, and exactly-24-hour cases. 2) Submit invalid interval/offset/timezone/duration cases. 3) Query with both filter boundaries, one missing boundary, reversed, and maximum/overmaximum range.
Expected Result: Valid inputs persist equivalent UTC instants and preserve display timezone. Past appointments are accepted. Invalid inputs are rejected. Filters require both endpoints, positive interval, and at most 366 days.

Title: Concurrent overlap exclusion and adjacency
Preconditions: Disposable PostgreSQL test database with proposed migration applied; two synchronized API clients; no production data.
Test Data: Same employee intervals [10:00,11:00) and [10:30,11:30); adjacent [11:00,12:00); distinct employee with [10:30,11:30).
Steps: 1) Submit two overlapping creates concurrently for one employee using distinct idempotency keys. 2) Query committed appointments and audit rows. 3) Create adjacent interval. 4) Create same-time interval for another employee.
Expected Result: Exactly one overlapping create commits; the other returns 409 appointment_overlap; no partial write/audit is left. Adjacent same-employee interval and overlapping different-employee interval succeed. Test only against disposable data.

Title: Appointment reschedule, cancellation, and terminal state
Preconditions: Runtime API with scheduled appointment, current ETag, archived client and inactive employee fixtures available.
Test Data: Valid reschedule; overlapping reschedule; cancellation-only PATCH; later patch after cancellation; stale/missing ETag.
Steps: 1) Reschedule with valid current ETag. 2) Attempt colliding reschedule and re-read. 3) Cancel and verify interval released. 4) PATCH cancelled appointment again. 5) Test cancellation when referenced client is archived/employee inactive.
Expected Result: Valid reschedule succeeds. Collision preserves prior booking/version. Cancellation succeeds and is terminal; subsequent patch returns 409. Cancellation is permitted despite archived client/inactive employee; missing/stale preconditions cause no change.

Title: Report permissions, exact metrics, and interval boundaries
Preconditions: Runtime API and disposable deterministic dataset with records before/at/inside/after boundaries and varied current states.
Test Data: Synthetic clients, deals, tasks, appointments; ranges from/to at UTC boundaries; admin/manager/employee sessions.
Steps: 1) Independently calculate expected six metrics. 2) Request summary as admin and manager. 3) Request as employee. 4) Try missing, reversed, zero, and >366-day intervals. 5) Reopen task/deal or cancel appointment and repeat.
Expected Result: Admin/manager values exactly match current-state definitions and UTC [from,to) bounds, including currency and generated_at. Employee is denied with 403. Invalid intervals are rejected. Current-state changes may alter historical-period metrics as documented.

Title: AI allowlist and authorization-scoped retrieval
Preconditions: AI integration implemented with a non-production provider/mock, synthetic fixture set, and request/tool logging that excludes secrets.
Test Data: Allowed lookup/list/summary/report requests; unsupported export/role-change/message requests; employee and manager identities; 20-row retrieval limit.
Steps: 1) Submit one allowed intent per role. 2) Submit prompts asking for unsupported tools or broader scope. 3) Inspect retrieval queries, outbound payload, tool configuration, and database/provider calls.
Expected Result: Only documented intents execute; data retrieval applies the authenticated actor’s permissions and bounds before model context. Unsupported requests cause no protected retrieval or write. No SQL, shell, arbitrary URL, generic HTTP, or database tool is exposed.

Title: Malformed, extra-field, semantically invalid, and ungrounded AI outputs
Preconditions: AI orchestrator available with deterministic mock provider and synthetic source records.
Test Data: Malformed JSON; missing required key; unknown key; unsupported schema_version/intent; invented/stale source ref; duplicate action; fabricated report total.
Steps: 1) Configure mock provider to return each invalid candidate. 2) Request a read-only summary referencing an unauthorized/nonretrieved record. 3) Return a report explanation with totals differing from reporting service. 4) Inspect result and persistence.
Expected Result: Invalid candidates fail closed or request clarification within documented call limits; no invalid candidate reaches mutation. Summaries only cite authorized retrieved handles; authoritative totals match report service, never model text.

Title: AI proposal confirmation, binding, replay, and one-time execution
Preconditions: AI proposal/status API and UI implemented on disposable database; task and appointment fixtures; controllable clock; synthetic accounts only.
Test Data: Valid task and appointment candidates; altered arguments; second actor; expired proposal; changed permission/version; concurrent duplicate confirmation.
Steps: 1) Create each proposal and verify no business row exists before confirmation. 2) Confirm once and inspect result/audit. 3) Repeat confirmation concurrently and sequentially. 4) Try altered arguments, another actor, expired proposal, and revoked permission/version.
Expected Result: No write occurs without confirmation. Only original actor can confirm unchanged, unexpired proposal after reauthorization. One successful confirmation creates exactly one record and audit entry; all invalid/replayed variants create no additional mutation.

Title: AI and persistence failures preserve manual CRM path
Preconditions: AI and manual CRM routes available in isolated test environment; controllable mock provider and database/audit fault injection.
Test Data: Provider timeout, 429, malformed response, database outage, audit write failure; valid manual client/task create.
Steps: 1) Trigger each AI/provider failure. 2) Inspect response, database, audit, and UI status. 3) Submit a manual CRM create while provider remains unavailable. 4) Retry any uncertain create only with same key/proposal.
Expected Result: No AI failure is reported as success and no partial mutation persists. Manual authenticated operation remains available during provider outage. No unbounded retry or duplicate mutation occurs; error state is explicit.

Title: Credential and bearer-token storage/log exposure
Preconditions: Runtime app, disposable database, and sanitized log access available; test account and session issued with synthetic values.
Test Data: Synthetic password and bearer token; database and application/ingress logs; HTTPS and local-development configurations.
Steps: 1) Authenticate over configured non-production HTTPS. 2) Inspect user/session storage and logs. 3) Search responses, URLs, browser storage, prompts, and logs for exact synthetic secrets. 4) Confirm production profile rejects plaintext transport.
Expected Result: Password stored as unique-salt Argon2id hash; session token stored only as hash; no secret appears in URLs, logs, prompts, or response beyond issued access token. Production profile requires HTTPS. Any leakage is a security defect.

Title: Malformed request, body limit, and safe problem responses
Preconditions: Runtime API available in isolated environment with read/write fixture and ability to inspect persisted state.
Test Data: Malformed JSON; unknown field; non-JSON content type; body exactly 65,536 bytes and 65,537 bytes; invalid enum; control characters.
Steps: 1) Send each invalid request to a representative read/write operation. 2) Record status/content type/problem fields. 3) Verify data state and scan response for secrets, SQL, stack traces, and protected record content.
Expected Result: Documented 400/413/415/422 responses use application/problem+json with request ID and safe fields. Invalid write requests make no mutation. Oversize body is rejected at the documented limit; no sensitive detail is exposed.

Title: Inert rendering and configured-origin CORS
Preconditions: Frontend implementation and test browser available; configured and unconfigured origins; synthetic record/AI text only.
Test Data: Text ``; script-like string; one allowed origin and one unconfigured origin.
Steps: 1) Display hostile synthetic text in client, task, and AI answer fields. 2) Verify no script execution and text remains inert. 3) Send CORS preflight/request from allowed and unconfigured origins.
Expected Result: Hostile strings render as inert text with no execution. Only configured frontend origin receives the declared CORS permission. No client-side restriction is treated as server authorization.

Title: Approved authentication and API rate-limit boundaries
Preconditions: Rate limits implemented with controllable clock; approved limits/windows recorded; isolated test accounts/IP identities.
Test Data: Login failed attempts: five per account+IP/15 min and 30 per IP/min; authenticated 120/min; AI 20/min/actor only if approved and implemented.
Steps: 1) Submit requests up to each approved limit. 2) Submit one additional request within the active window. 3) Advance test clock past window and retry. 4) Inspect status, Retry-After, account-enumeration behavior, and business effects.
Expected Result: Within-limit requests follow normal behavior; over-limit request returns 429 with Retry-After and no protected action. Login responses do not reveal account existence. If values remain unapproved or route is absent, leave Not Run and record the decision blocker.

Title: Idempotent create replay, key mismatch, and conditional update
Preconditions: Runtime API/database available in isolated environment; supported create endpoint; current ETag; audit/idempotency inspection.
Test Data: Same UUID key and same body; same key and changed body; concurrent same-key requests; missing/stale/wildcard/multi-tag If-Match.
Steps: 1) POST same create twice with identical key/body. 2) Repeat same key with changed body. 3) Race two identical requests. 4) PATCH with missing, stale, wildcard, multi-tag, and current ETags. 5) Inspect rows and audit records.
Expected Result: Same-key/same-body replay returns original authorized result and produces one resource; changed body conflicts; concurrent requests do not duplicate. PATCH preconditions follow 428/400/412/current success semantics without unintended writes.

Title: Database and audit outage do not create success-shaped state
Preconditions: Disposable database and fault-injection hooks available; no production data; manual CRM API and AI mock available.
Test Data: Injected DB outage; audit insert failure; provider outage; ordinary manual request.
Steps: 1) Inject DB outage during create. 2) Restore DB and inject audit failure during create. 3) Trigger provider outage. 4) Inspect API response and database after each. 5) Submit manual CRM request during provider outage.
Expected Result: Database/audit failure returns explicit server/dependency error and leaves no partial business row/replay success. Provider outage disables only AI; manual API operation works. No success message appears before commit is known.

Title: Proposed non-AI p95 target benchmark
Preconditions: Implemented API and approved benchmark profile; documented hardware/software; disposable synthetic dataset only; performance target formally accepted before judging pass/fail.
Test Data: 20 concurrent synthetic users; 1,000 synthetic clients; approved endpoint mix and warm-up; non-AI requests only.
Steps: 1) Confirm written approval of the proposed profile and workload. 2) Run the same benchmark at least three times with no concurrent development load. 3) Save sanitized raw summaries and environment. 4) Report p50/p95/p99 and failures; measure AI separately.
Expected Result: Until target and workload are approved and API exists, status remains Not Run. If approved, target passes only when non-AI p95 <500 ms with failures reported and no excluded slow requests; no result is inferred from contract checks.

Title: UI states for loading, empty, validation, denial, conflict, and outage
Preconditions: Frontend implementation or reviewable prototype available; mock server can return documented response codes.
Test Data: Mock 200 empty/list, 400/401/403/404/409/412/422/429/500/503 responses; pending request; unknown commit result.
Steps: 1) Exercise list loading and empty states. 2) Inject each error and pending/uncertain mutation response. 3) Observe displayed outcome and available recovery actions.
Expected Result: Each state is visibly distinguishable; no failed/unknown mutation is presented as successful. Recovery matches documented semantics: reauthenticate, refetch after 412, retry create with same idempotency key, or use manual form after AI failure.

Title: Appointment timezone and daylight-saving ambiguity presentation
Preconditions: Appointment UI implemented; timezone database available; synthetic test data only.
Test Data: A valid UTC date; Asia/Qyzylorda +05:00; a DST zone with one ambiguous local time and one nonexistent local time.
Steps: 1) Enter normal and boundary local times. 2) Attempt to proceed with ambiguous/nonexistent time. 3) Resolve the time if supported. 4) Inspect displayed timezone, offset, UTC instant, and AI proposal confirmation.
Expected Result: Ambiguous/nonexistent time is explicitly resolved or rejected. Before submit/confirm, final local time, timezone, offset, and instant are visible. Changed times require a fresh AI proposal confirmation.

Title: Approved accessibility conformance assessment
Preconditions: Stakeholder decision records required conformance level and workflow scope; frontend pages and supported-browser matrix available.
Test Data: All MVP login, list, form, error, report, appointment, and AI confirmation workflows; keyboard and assistive-technology checks.
Steps: 1) Confirm whether WCAG 2.2 AA is approved. 2) If approved, run automated scan and manual keyboard/screen-reader checks on agreed pages. 3) Record each violation and retest corrections.
Expected Result: Until a conformance target is approved, no compliance conclusion is reported. If WCAG 2.2 AA is approved, report all scoped findings; unresolved Level A/AA failures prevent meeting the proposed criterion.

Title: Requirement/API contract validator
Preconditions: Clean checkout of the tested commit; locked Node dependencies installed with npm ci --ignore-scripts.
Test Data: Command: npm run validate:api; package-lock.json dependency versions.
Steps: 1) Run npm ci --ignore-scripts from repository root. 2) Run npm run validate:api. 3) Capture command, commit, and complete exit/output.
Expected Result: Static validator exits 0 and reports OpenAPI 3.0.3, 17 paths, 27 operations, 225 example occurrences, six invalid fixtures rejected, and selected auth/retry/precondition/error/pagination/response checks. This validates the contract only, not runtime behavior.

Title: Relational constraints and persisted business invariants
Preconditions: Disposable migrated PostgreSQL database and application implementation available; never run against production.
Test Data: Invalid foreign key; inactive client/user; malformed amount; immutable client linkage; duplicate email; overlapping appointment; valid precision values.
Steps: 1) Submit invalid relationships and boundary values directly to API/database service. 2) Attempt immutable-field changes. 3) Attempt overlapping appointment create and update. 4) Verify valid records and database state after each attempt.
Expected Result: Persistence layer rejects invalid references/invariants even when bypassing browser validation; valid exact amounts round-trip without precision loss; rejected operations do not corrupt previously valid state.

Title: AI provider data minimization and real-data gate
Preconditions: AI integration with mock provider, outbound request capture, synthetic records; provider privacy review documented before any real-data use.
Test Data: Synthetic client contact fields, authorized task/deal rows, session token canary, password canary, audit/auth records.
Steps: 1) Run every supported AI intent with synthetic data. 2) Capture outbound payloads and logs. 3) Search for excluded secrets/contact fields and unauthorized records. 4) Verify provider/retention approval gate blocks real-data configuration if review is missing.
Expected Result: Only minimum allowed fields and authorized bounded records are sent. Passwords, tokens, provider keys, auth/audit data, raw prompt by default, and unrelated contacts are absent. Real-data use is disabled until processing/retention/region/deletion review is documented.

Title: Mutation audit atomicity, denial event, and redaction
Preconditions: Runtime database/audit path and restricted event sink available in a disposable environment.
Test Data: One successful synthetic create; forbidden cross-owner request; injected audit-storage failure; secret canaries in input.
Steps: 1) Commit a valid mutation and inspect associated audit fields. 2) Perform forbidden operation and inspect denial event with no business write. 3) Inject mutation-audit failure and retry in isolation. 4) Search logs/audit for secret canaries.
Expected Result: Committed mutation has one linked audit event with actor/action/object/time/outcome/request ID. Audit failure rolls back business change. Denial is observed via restricted event path but creates no business mutation. Secrets and full personal payloads are redacted.
